Chef Maurice Levene, or “Chef Moe,” as he’s known on TikTok, isn’t your typical culinary creator. With nearly a quarter century in the culinary field and eight years experience as head chef, he’s using his expertise about the art and science of cooking to help his viewers cook good meals, on a budget. Levene launched his TikTok account last year to share cooking tips, but he soon learned some of his followers were struggling to afford basic necessities. “There was one message in particular of someone expressing how they thought the dish was amazing. They couldn’t wait to try it, but they had to wait till next month to buy the ingredients to make the dish,” said Levene.  And just like that, the Mount Pocono, Pennsylvania-based chef launched a new budget-conscious series on his channel: How to feed a family with just $5 or $10 dollars. “Instead of just showing how to make the dish. Why don’t we explain why we’re doing this and this for the dish so that we’ll build the confidence in people so they could be able to cook.” Levene walks his viewers through how to shop, prep and prepare a meal, while explaining the techniques chefs use to pair flavors, emulsify sauces and even how to create flavor without seasonings. “They didn’t have certain spices, something that I take for granted, you take for granted and we wouldn’t think how somebody couldn’t have salt and pepper or someone couldn’t have paprika. And that really, that was my eye opening moment that people need help.” According to the Department of Agriculture, food prices have risen 3.2 percent in the last year. An Urban Institute study found, nearly a third of working-age adults living with children reported food insecurity last year. With over 800 thousand followers on TikTok, and growing, Chef Moe hopes his videos can help familes get food on the table and build confidence around the world. “I’m not going to stop World Hunger, but if I can help a few people. Crispy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Wraps🍗🧀🌯 The flavours are absolutely phenomenal, one of the best wraps made using a sheet pan. Low effort, minimal cleanup and incredibly delicious🔥 Great to serve for large groups/gatherings at home Macros Per Wrap (10 Total) 423 Calories | 41g Protein | 25g Carbs | 18g Fat Ingredients (Makes 10 Wraps) Garlic Parmesan Chicken - 600g Raw Boneless Skinless Chicken Thighs, cut into cubes - 600g Raw Chicken Breast, cut into cubes - 2.5 Tsp Salt - 2 Tsp Chilli Flakes - 3 Tsp Parsley - 4 Tsp Italian Herbs - 3 Tsp Paprika - 4 Tsp Garlic Granules or Powder - 200g Grated Parmesan - 6 Tsp Olive Oil - Avocado Cooking Spray (use before baking) Garlic Pamesan Creamy Sauce - 350g Light Evaporated Milk - 2 Tsp Italian Herbs - 1 Tsp Garlic Powder - 1 Tsp Paprika - 80g Grated Parmesan - 100g Light Cream Cheese - 15g Light Butter Wraps & Filling - 10 Low Carb Wraps (Brand: Mission) - Shredded Lettuce - Chopped Tomatoes - Chopped Onions 👨‍🍳 Cooking Instructions 1. Slice chicken breast and thighs into cubes. Add seasonings with grated parmesan cheese and drizzle of olive oil. Mix until well coated. 2. In a pan on low heat, add light butter with seasonings. Toast for a minute before adding evaporated milk, extra Parmesan and cream cheese. Stir till smooth and creamy. 3. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper, spread marinated chicken evenly (do not overcrowd), add light layer of cooking spray then bake in a preheated oven for 20-22 mins at 200C until crispy. 4. While chicken is still hot, add extra parmesan and parsley. Mix well until coated and extra cheesy. 5. Assemble the wraps with shredded lettuce, onion, tomato, crispy chicken and sauce. ENJOY! Storage and Reheating Tips - Store chicken and creamy sauce in separate containers in the fridge. - When ready to eat, just warm up chicken in oven/air fryer for 4-5 mins 180C / 370F. Crockpot Mongolian Beef & Noodles 🥩🍜🔥 Crockpot Series Episode 7: Mongolian Beef & Noodles This is my crockpot series, where I help you make easy recipes so good you might find a spouse or impress the one you’ve got. Tender chuck roast, a sweet and savory Mongolian-style sauce, and noodles coated in all that flavor. We sear the beef for extra color, then the crockpot does the work and you take the credit! 🙌🏽🔥 Ingredients: 2 pounds thinly sliced chuck roast 4 tablespoons butter, for searing 1 cup low-sodium shoyu 1 cup brown sugar 1 cup low-sodium beef broth 2 tablespoons minced garlic 1 tablespoon grated ginger 2 tablespoon sesame oil 2 tablespoons rice vinegar 1 teaspoon black pepper 2 tablespoons cornstarch 2 tablespoons cold water 12 ounces precooked lo mein noodles. I used yakisoba noodles brand is Fortune. Sliced green onions Sesame seeds, optional Instructions: 1. Season your beef with SPG or your favorite seasoning. Heat a skillet over high heat with the butter and sear the beef in small batches for 1-2 minutes per side. You’re building color, not cooking it through. 2. Transfer the beef to the crockpot. Deglaze the skillet with a splash of the measured beef broth, scrape up those browned bits, and pour everything into the crockpot. 3. Add the remaining broth, shoyu, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and black pepper. Stir gently. 4. Cover and cook on LOW for 4 to 5 hours or HIGH for 2.5 to 3.5 hours. Start checking early so the thin beef stays tender without falling apart. 5. Mix the cornstarch slurry with a cup of broth. Stir the slurry into the sauce and cook on HIGH for 15–20 minutes, until thick and glossy. 6. Slice the green onions into 1 inch piece. Separate the precooked noodles and add them directly to the crockpot. Toss everything together and heat on HIGH for 5–10 minutes. 7. Finish with sliced green onions, sesame seeds, and chili crisp oil if you want some heat then serve immediately. Don’t leave those noodles sitting on KEEP WARM—they’ll keep drinking up the sauce. Save this one for an easy weeknight dinner! 🍜🔥 #crockpotrecipes #crockpot #EasyRecipe #hawaiitiktok #mongolianbeef

videos.caption: Steak Cheese and Rice is easy to make and never disappoints! 🌮 INGREDIENTS  1 1/2 lbs Sirloin or New York Strip steak, sliced thin  1/2 tsp each salt and pepper 1 tsp each cumin, dried cilantro, garlic powder, onion powder 2 tsp chili powder 2 cups Jasmine rice rinsed  2 tbsp olive oil divided  1 small onion chopped 3 cups chicken broth 1 tbsp tomato Bouillon  1 1/2 cups White Queso 1 tbsp Fresh Cilantro 1 package Fajita size flour tortillas INSTRUCTIONS  Slice 1 1/2 lbs of steak into thin pieces. Add your sliced steak to a bowl with 1 tbsp olive oil. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, dried cilantro, garlic powder, onion powder, and chili powder. Stir until steak is well coated in seasoning and oil. Set aside.   Rinse 2 cups of Jasmine rice. Add rice to a skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp of olive oil and stir the rice around the skillet letting it toast up for 4-5 minutes.  Add the chopped onion and tomato bouillon to the skillet. Stir well. Add 3 cups of chicken broth. Stir well and let cook until it starts bubbling.  Once the whole skillet is bubbling, cover with a lid, lower the heat to medium low, and let cook for about 18 minutes or until rice is tender.   While the rice is cooking, heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the steak until it is cooked to your liking. I cooked the steak for about 10 minutes. Remove it from the heat.  Top the cooked rice with the steak and pour white queso over the skillet of steak and rice. Top with fresh cilantro. Serve as is or inside of flour tortillas.  #easyrecipes #dinner #steak

Recipe Name: Slow Cooker Creamy Garlic Parmesan Pork Chops Ingredients 1. 4 bone-in pork chops 2. 1 tsp salt 3. 1/2 tsp black pepper 4. 1 tsp garlic powder 5. 1 tsp onion powder 6. 1 tbsp olive oil 7. 3 tbsp butter 8. 4 cloves garlic, minced 9. 1 cup chicken broth 10. 1 cup heavy cream 11. 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese 12. 1 tsp Italian seasoning 13. 1/2 tsp paprika 14. 1 tbsp cornstarch 15. 2 tbsp water 16. 2 tbsp chopped parsley Recipe 1. Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels. 2. Season both sides with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika. 3. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. 4. Sear the pork chops for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown. 5. Transfer the pork chops to a slow cooker. 6. In the same skillet, melt butter and sauté the garlic for 30 seconds. 7. Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the pan. 8. Stir in the heavy cream, Parmesan cheese, and Italian seasoning. 9. Pour the creamy mixture over the pork chops in the slow cooker. 10. Cover and cook on LOW for 5–6 hours or HIGH for 2½–3 hours. 11. Mix cornstarch and water in a small bowl until smooth. 12. Stir the slurry into the slow cooker during the last 20 minutes of cooking. 13. Let the sauce thicken while the pork chops finish cooking. 14. Spoon the creamy garlic Parmesan sauce over the pork chops. 15. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving. 16. Serve hot with mashed potatoes, rice, or roasted vegetables. Crispy garlic parmesan chicken rolls Ingredients  For the chicken: 2 lb boneless chicken breast, cut into small pieces  Salt to taste 1 tsp black pepper  1 tbsp garlic powder  1 tsp onion powder  2 tsp paprika powder  1/2 tsp cumin powder  1 tbsp lemon juice  1 tbsp oil (for marinating) 1 small yellow onion, diced 1 red bell pepper, diced 2 tbsp oil for cooking  For the garlic parmesan sauce: 1 tbsp butter  1 tbsp garlic, minced  1 1/2 cup unsweetened heavy whipping cream 1 tbsp cream cheese  Salt to taste 1/2 tsp black pepper  1 tsp garlic powder  1 tsp red chili flakes  1 cup Parmesan cheese , freshly grated  1 tsp parsley , finely chopped  To assemble: 9-10 small flour tortilla wraps 1 cup mozzarella cheese  Oil for pan frying  Method: Season chicken with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cumin, lemon juice, and oil. Mix well. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken until fully cooked and lightly golden. Add diced onion and bell pepper and sauté for 2–3 minutes until softened. Set aside. For the sauce, melt butter over medium-low heat. Add garlic and sauté for 30 seconds. Add heavy cream, cream cheese, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and red chili flakes. Whisk until smooth and simmer until slightly thickened. Lower the heat and stir in Parmesan until melted and smooth. Turn off the heat and add parsley. Reserve half the sauce for dipping and mix the remaining half with the chicken. Let cool slightly. Add a few spoonfuls of filling to each tortilla and sprinkle with mozzarella. Fold in the sides and roll tightly. Lightly oil a skillet over medium to medium-low heat. Place rolls seam-side down and cook, turning until golden and crispy on all sides. Add more oil as needed. Avoid high heat so the tortilla doesn't brown before the cheese melts. Mango Fruit Cakes wie von Cedric Grolet🥭 •Für die Fruchtfüllung: - 300g Mangopüree aus 100% Mango - 180g frische, reife, süße Mango (in kleine Würfel geschnitten) - 25g Zucker - 3,5g Pektin NH - 15g Glukosesirup - 10g frisch ausgedrückter Limettensaft  - 2 Vanilleschooten  Zucker und Pektin mischen Die 25 g Zucker mit den 3,5 g Pektin NH gründlich trocken vermischen. Dadurch wird verhindert, dass das Pektin beim Einrühren Klümpchen bildet. Mangopüree erwärmen Die 300 g Mangopüree und das Mark der Vanilleschooten in einen kleinen Topf geben und eventuell kurz mit einem Stabmixer vermischen, sodass sich das Mark verteilen kann und dann ungefähr 40–45 °C erwärmen. Es soll warm sein, aber noch nicht kochen. Pektin einarbeiten Während du das Mangopüree mit einem Schneebesen ständig rührst, die Zucker-Pektin-Mischung langsam einrieseln lassen.Anschließend die 15 g Glukosesirup dazugeben und alles unter Rühren weiter erhitzen.Kurz aufkochen Die Masse einmal richtig aufkochen lassen. Sobald sie sichtbar zu blubbern beginnt, ungefähr 1 Minute leicht sprudelnd kochen lassen, dabei ständig rühren. Limettensaft hinzufügen Den Topf vom Herd nehmen und die 10 g Limettensaft gründlich einrühren. Mangowürfel unterheben. Die Masse etwas abkühlen lassen, bis sie nicht mehr kochend heiß ist. Anschließend die 180 g frischen Mangowürfel unterheben. Die Würfel sollten ungefähr 5–8 mm groß sein, damit sie später beim Anschneiden schön sichtbar sind. Silikonformen befüllen und einfrieren. Die Mango-Fruchtfüllung in die Silikonformen füllen und vollständig durchfrieren lassen, am besten über Nacht. Anschließend die gefrorenen Mango-Inserts vorsichtig aus den Formen lösen und bis zur Weiterverwendung in Gefrierschrank tun, damit sie ja nicht auftauen.  •Für die Vanille-Whipped- Ganache: - 400g Schlagsahne - 170g kalte Schlagsahne - 2 Vanilleschooten - 2 TL Vanilleextrakt - 2 Blatt Rindergelatine - 140g weiße Kuvertüre (gehackt) - 140g Mascarpone Die Gelatine in kaltem Wasser einweichen und 5 Minuten quellen lassen. 400 g Sahne zusammen mit dem Mark der Vanilleschoten erhitzen, bis die Sahne heiß ist, aber nicht kocht.Vom Herd nehmen und die eingeweichte Gelatine darin vollständig auflösen. Die heiße Vanillesahne über die weiße Schokolade und den Mascarpone gießen.Kurz 2 Minuten stehen lassen und anschließend fein pürieren oder glatt verrühren. Die 170 g kalte Sahne hinzufügen und erneut mixen, bis eine glatte Masse entsteht. Abgedeckt mindestens 6 Stunden, besser über Nacht, im Kühlschrank durchkühlen lassen. Die Ganache anschließend aufschlagen, bis sie mittlere bis feste Spitzen bildet, und direkt verwenden. Die vollständig gefrorene Mango-Fruchtfüllung vorsichtig auf ein Messer oder einen stabilen Spieß stecken und in die Whipped Ganache tunken. Dabei hin und her bewegen und drehen, bis jede Stelle gleichmäßig bedeckt ist. Die Schicht sollte weder zu dick noch zu dünn sein. Überschüssige Ganache durch leichtes Abklopfen am Schüsselrand entfernen und die Form bei Bedarf vorsichtig korrigieren. Die Ganache kurz anziehen lassen, die Fruchtfüllung vorsichtig vom Messer lösen und auf einen mit Backpapier belegten Teller legen. Anschließend ungefähr 1 Stunde einfrieren, bis die Ganache fest ist.Danach Handschuhe anziehen und die Früchte vorsichtig mit den Händen in Form bringen. Durch die Handwärme wird die Oberfläche minimal weicher und lässt sich schön glätten. Dabei zügig arbeiten, damit die Früchte nicht zu stark antauen. Anschließend erneut ungefähr 1 Stunde einfrieren, bis alles vollständig fest ist. Danach können die Früchte mit der Schokoladen-Kakaobutter-Mischung überzogen werden. •Für den Schokoladen Überzug: - 150g Kakaobutter - 200g weiße Kuvertüre von Callebaut - ölbasierte Lebensmittelfarbe Mango Colormill Schokolade + Kakaobutter in der Mikrowelle schmelzen (alle 30 Sek.rühren) Temperatur: 38 °C • Außerdem: - Velly Spray grün und rot  Nach dem Sprühen, kurz trocknen lassen.  Das Rezept ergibt 6 Stück. 4 Stunden vor Verzehr im Kühlschrank auftauen lassen. Gutes Gelingen.

Creamy Tuscan White Beans Ingredients (4-5 servings): • 2 (15-oz) cans white beans, Great Northern or cannellini, drained and rinsed • 1½ cups cherry tomatoes, halved • ⅓ cup sun-dried tomatoes, chopped • 1 small yellow onion, finely diced • 4 garlic cloves, finely minced • 1 tbsp olive oil • 1 tsp Italian seasoning • ½ tsp smoked paprika • ¼ tsp red pepper flakes, plus more to taste • 1 tbsp all-purpose flour • 1½ cups broth • ½ cup whole milk • 1 tsp Dijon mustard • ½ cup finely grated Parmesan, plus more for serving • 2–3 cups chopped kale, tough stems removed • 1 tbsp lemon juice • 1 tsp honey • ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper • Salt, to taste • Extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing • Crusty sourdough, for serving Instructions: 1. Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the olive oil and diced onion with a pinch of salt. Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly golden. 2. Add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they’re blistered and beginning to collapse. Reserve some of the blistered tomatoes for later. 3. Add garlic and sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 30-60 seconds until fragrant.  4. Stir in Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, red pepper flakes and black pepper. 5. Sprinkle flour over everything and stir for about 30 seconds. Slowly pour in the broth while stirring, followed by the milk and Dijon mustard. 6. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. 7. Stir in the beans and simmer gently for 5–7 minutes.  8. Mash about ⅓ of the beans against the side of the skillet with the back of a spoon. 9. Stir in the chopped kale, cover, and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring once or twice, until tender but still vibrant. 10. Lower the heat and stir in the Parmesan until melted and glossy. 11. Add lemon juice and honey. Taste and adjust salt, pepper and red pepper flakes. If the sauce is thicker than you want, stir in a splash of broth. 12. Top with the reserved blistered tomatoes, Parmesan, black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Enjoy! #beans #whitebeans #fallrecipes #easydinner #dinneridea
